alignments.note: Explicit subject takes only its own English (rule 20).
Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate noun (rule 20). The ASV italic on 'was' corroborates the supply but does not make it added (rule 7).

One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase; head on the lexeme-bearing 'first', since 'fruits' alone is any fruits (rule 31). The rectum carries a suffix and no article, so the 'the' is supplied on the construct (rule 29).
Anarthrous participle used substantivally; the supplied relative joins its unit and the head stays on the lexeme (rule 46).

אָשַׁם rendered by a light verb plus adjectival complement: 'shall be guilty' keeps the lexeme and 'shall be held' loses it, so rule 31's subtraction puts the head on 'guilty' under rule 44, as with בּוֹשׁ -> 'put to shame'. Rule 24's preference for the lexical predicate is about 'was gathered' and must not be read as a preference for the English verb; heading on 'held' is the reading corrected here.
The oracle formula noun is rendered verbally; the ASV writes no 'of', so rule 19 has nothing to place.

review_notes: Corrected the target head of s011 from 'held' to 'guilty': 'be held guilty' is a light verb plus complement and rule 44's subtraction puts the lexeme of אָשַׁם in 'guilty'. This also brings the verse into line with the chapter's own reading of רָחֲקוּ -> 'are gone far' and יֶּהְבָּלוּ -> 'are become vain' in JER.2.5.
'first fruits' headed on 'first' by rule 31's subtraction test; unit edges unchanged.
All other units verified and retained unchanged; every s### and t### is partitioned exactly once.
